1 G.A.

HON'BLE RAJ BEER SINGH, J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

This application under Section 528 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (hereinafter referred to as 'BNSS') has been filed for quashing of the entire proceedings, including charge-sheet dated 24.11.2021 as well as cognizance / summoning order dated 16.05.2023, of Case No. 376 of 2023 (State Vs. Vinod Kumar), arising out of Case Crime No.653 of 2021, under Sections 323, 504, 506,
308 IPC, P.S.- Soraon, District- Prayagraj, pending in the court of A.C.J. (J.D.)-11, Allahabad.
3.
It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

The first information report was lodged under Sections 323,
504, 506 IPC against applicant and two co-accused persons.

Learned counsel has referred first information report and statement of eye-witness Pooja and Usha and submitted that they have not stated any such fact that injured were assaulted with any hard or blunt object, whereas in medical examination report of injured Nisha Devi one abrasion has been shown, besides traumatic swelling and complaint of pain.
Thus, the medical evidence does not corroborate prosecution version and the incident is doubtful.

It was further submitted that as per report of radiologist, fracture was shown in temporal bone of injured Nisha Devi, which is not possible without use of any weapon / object but the eye-witness has not stated that any weapon was used.
Referring to facts of the matter, it was submitted that impugned proceedings are liable to be quashed.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the application and submitted that in view of allegations made in first information report and materials on record, a prima-facie case is made out against applicants.
5. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

6. The legal position on the issue of quashing of criminal proceedings is well-settled that the jurisdiction to quash a complaint, FIR or a charge-sheet should be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.

However, where the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and material on record even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused, the charge-sheet may be quashed in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

In well celebrated judgement reported in AIR 1992 SC 605 State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal, Supreme Court has carved out certain guidelines, wherein FIR or proceedings may be quashed but cautioned that the power to quash FIR or proceedings should be exercised sparingly and that too in the rarest of rare cases.

sentences.text: It has been held that if a prima facie case is made out disclosing ingredients of the offence, court should not quash the charge sheet/complaint.
It is equally well settled that at this stage questions of fact cannot be examined and a mini trial cannot be held.

7. In the instant matter the informant has made clear allegations that on 27.10.2021 at about 09:00 AM on account of dispute over drainage, applicant and co-accused persons have assaulted the informant with legs and shoes and she was hit at her abdomen.
It was further alleged that when informant's neighbours, namely, Usha Devi, Sunita and Pooja tried to save the informant, they were also assaulted by the accused persons.

In injury report of informant / injured Nisha, one abrasion,
one traumatic swelling and one complaint of pain have been shown and as per report of radiologist,
fracture was shown in temporal bone.
The injured has supported prosecution version in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

It is correct that in the first information report or in the statement of injured and eye-witnesses recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., there is no such allegation that accused persons have assaulted the injured with any specific weapon or by blunt weapon but considering nature of injuries, it can not be said that such injuries are not possible when the injured is attacked with legs and shoes.
In view of material on record, it can not be said that no prima-facie case is made out against applicant.

The submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicant call for determination on questions of fact, which may adequately be discerned /
adjudicated only by the trial court.
Even the submissions made on point of law can also be more appropriately gone into by the trial court.
Adjudication of questions of facts and appreciation of evidence or examining the reliability and credibility of the version, does not fall within the arena of jurisdiction under Section 528 BNSS.

8. After considering arguments raised by learned counsel for the parties and perusing the impugned first information report and materials on record, no case for quashing of impugned proceedings is made out.
The application under Section 528 BNSS lacks merits and thus, liable to be dismissed.
9. Accordingly, the application u/s 528 BNSS is dismissed.

(Raj Beer Singh,J.) September 2, 2025 'SP'/-
